From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Prepay bucket velocity question

Hi Maya,

Thanks for the clear ask. Ive attached a proposal that outlines two options for smoothing a prepay wallet when you expect an early ramp:

1) Tiered velocity smoothing: maintain a fixed monthly drawdown percentage but apply an "early ramp buffer" that releases an additional fixed % from a reserve in months 1-6, then rebalances months 7-12. This preserves predictable monthly costs and keeps the visible consumption curve flatter.

2) Weighted true-up cadence: frontload up to 30% in month 1, but enforce a monthly true-up at month-ends with an automatic smoothing credit applied across remaining months of the year (so accounting sees a linearized expense). This requires a contract clause for amortization of the prepay.

Attached: Redwood_Prepay_Proposal_v3.xlsx (has sample amortization table) and a one-page Commitment_Bucket_Schedule.pdf with sample drawdown curves.

If useful, we can model your specific baseline to produce a month-by-month P&L smoothing table — I can ask Naomi to run the revenue recognition impact.

Next step: do you prefer the reserve-buffer approach or the weighted true-up?

Cheers,
Rachel

--
Rachel Kim
Senior Sales Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Quick notes from pricing:

- If Acme wants a smoothing/true-up that materially delays recognition of revenue, we should hold discount off the front-loaded portion (i.e., differentiate the 30% frontload vs. the amortized remainder). Suggest 10% additional discount on the committed baseline after year 1 if they commit to 3 years.
- Also propose a small overage credit rule for months where actual usage < forecasted usage (helps mitigate large visible underspend for them).

Happy to walk through the numbers live. This should preserve our margin while giving Acme better month-to-month visibility.

Ben
Account Director, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Oct 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Revenue recognition and accounting notes

Rachel/Ben,

I ran a quick revenue recognition mock for both approaches and attached my notes (RevenueRecognitionNotes.docx). Key points:

- The weighted true-up with monthly amortization maps cleanly to monthly recognized revenue, but legal needs a clause that permits amortization across the committed period to avoid revenue timing mismatch.
- Reserve-buffer approach is simpler contractually but creates a reserve liability on our books that requires monthly reclassification when buffer is released. Finance is fine with either but recommends the amortization clause for cleaner treatment.
- For a 3-year commitment, recommend a 24-month smoothing window after an initial 30% frontload to minimize hit in year 1 expense for the customer while keeping our revenue deferral manageable.

I also flagged the audit requirement: we should include a monthly usage report delivery (CSV) and an API endpoint for reconciliation to satisfy their SOC/finance team.

-N
